title: Max Clark: opening his own boxing gym at 18
summary: On the PT Launch Lab Podcast, Ryan Robinson sits down with Max Clark, the young boxer and coach who has just opened Clark's Boxing Academy in Normanton. Max went to boxing behind his mum's back for two years, started holding pads for clients in his back garden at 15, and qualified through an apprenticeship before opening his own gym. They talk about what age kids should start boxing, Max's 19-fight record and plans to turn pro, and why showing client progress beats posting yourself. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Royal Marines to personal trainer: Jerome Scherrer
summary: Jerome Scherrer joined the Royal Marines as a teenager and spent most of his 20s and 30s there, then worked for the American government in Afghanistan before walking away from the money to become a personal trainer. Callum Brown talks to him about his Neverland Theory of leaving the military bubble, the first client he thrashed with nothing to show for it, and the six pillars framework he now uses with every client. Plus why he thinks 'bespoke programming' is mostly nonsense. Watch or read the full episode.

title: From 46 stone to qualified PT: Jack Atkinson
summary: Jack Atkinson weighed 46 and a half stone at his heaviest. Ryan and Callum talk to the former PT Launch Lab learner about the NHS scheme that didn't stick, the gastric surgery abroad that kick-started his weight loss, and the plateau at 31 stone that made him take ownership and get his own PT. Now qualified and coaching from a converted double garage, Jack explains why his niche is beginners and people too anxious to walk into a gym, and why before and after photos don't suit every client. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Gemma: from corporate job to personal trainer
summary: Gemma is a personal trainer from Saddleworth who qualified with PT Launch Lab after years managing sales teams and apprenticeships in the corporate world. She talks honestly with Callum about drinking, weight gain and the end of her marriage, the mindset work that turned things round and saw her lose 40 kilos, and how she now coaches busy working mums through her business, Phoenix Fitness Mindset. She also explains how she runs a hybrid online and face-to-face offer. Watch or read the full episode.

title: How running saved Matty Bell from addiction
summary: Matty Bell is a Pontefract running coach who turned to running after his addiction spiralled during COVID. He tells Ryan about the loneliness of early recovery, buying his first pair of running trainers, and how his local running club gave him a community of people who wanted to get better. He also explains how he coaches clients who drink at weekends, why every runner needs a race to train for, and why he qualified as a personal trainer to offer strength and conditioning for runners. Watch or read the full episode.

title: From ICU nurse to her own business: Maria's story
summary: Maria is a registered nurse and independent nurse prescriber who started her career in intensive care and multi-trauma before going it alone in aesthetics. She talks candidly with Callum and Ryan about what ICU taught her and the therapy that followed, building a business from scratch through daily self-promotion, and how she uses blood work and functional medicine with clients. They also cover the risks of GLP-1s without support and her three tips for lowering cortisol. Watch or read the full episode.

title: How Pembo got sober and became a boxing coach
summary: Pembo, founder of Pembo's Boxing & Fitness, left his delivery driving job to coach boxing full-time and runs a weekly class at Burns Bootcamp in Wakefield. He talks openly with Ryan Robinson about joining the army at 16, the drink and cocaine that followed, the night one reckless punch put a friend in hospital and became his rock bottom, and what nearly two years sober has changed. He also talks about the app he has built to help people stay sober. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Super League debut to open-heart surgery: Keal
summary: Keal made his Super League debut for Bradford Bulls at 17 and was twice named the best young player in the country at the Top Gun awards. Then a collapse mid-game revealed the narrowed heart valve he was born with and led to open-heart surgery. He talks openly about coming back, leaving full-time rugby to build his own mortgage and insurance business, the pancreatic tumour he was diagnosed with at 35, and why he is still turning up to work and the gym. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Kav: from the Army to Dizzee Rascal's stage to PT
summary: Kav grew up on the Gipton estate in Leeds, joined the Army with no qualifications and spent five years there, before a TikTok freestyle went viral and music put him on stage with Dizzee Rascal. He tells Ryan Robinson about losing his purpose after the Army, the drinking and partying that came with the music, and how training pulled him back. Now a newly qualified personal trainer, he shares his plans for outdoor group sessions and, one day, a warehouse gym with live music. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Marcus on addiction, recovery and Mean and Clean
summary: Marcus is the founder of Mean and Clean, a fitness-led recovery programme for people getting clean and sober. He tells Ryan Robinson about growing up obsessed with martial arts and the gym, the partying that took over, why he turned down antidepressants and built his recovery around training instead, and how a video he posted a month into getting clean reached 2.4 million views. He also talks, for the first time on camera, about finding faith two years into sobriety. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Laura: from competitive dancer to yoga studio owner
summary: Laura competed in dance at a high level, placing third in the world in her division, until degenerative disc disease in her back brought it to a sudden stop. Yoga and Pilates were part of her rehab and she fell in love with them. She tells Ryan Robinson about opening Vibe Yoga in Pontefract while still working full-time, building community through small classes, adapting yoga for every level, and how to step away from a day job safely. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Zac Meakin: from go-karts to British GT4 champion
summary: Zac Meakin is the racing driver Ryan Robinson has trained for around five years. He tells the story from his first go-kart laps in Pontefract to winning the British GT4 Championship with McLaren after a season of Porsche breakdowns, and explains success penalties, racing in the rain and what a factory driver actually is. He also talks about why he is working through his Level 3 personal training qualification alongside racing. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Luke McCarthy: Leeds United academy to pro Hyrox
summary: Luke McCarthy is a Hyrox athlete who turned pro after ranking second in the UK in the open category. He tells Ryan Robinson about six years in the Leeds United academy, being kicked out of school and growing up dyslexic, and swapping years of motocross injuries for running and Hyrox. He also opens up about three years of partying before he quit drinking, the 20-plus-hour training week he programmes for himself, and how all of it shapes the way he coaches. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Sam Hincks: the bodybuilding prep that broke him
summary: Sam Hincks started lifting at 13 on his dad's multi-gym and went on to win British powerlifting titles and a world championship. He tells Ryan about the bodybuilding prep that broke him six weeks out, ending in tears at a wedding breakfast and a secret sweet stash hidden around the house, and the second prep where he stepped on stage and won two classes while working 40 hours a week. They also talk about toxic social media, expensive coaching gurus and his move into Hyrox. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Ridge Holland on rugby league, WWE and what came next
summary: Miles catches up with Luke Menzies, the Yorkshire rugby league player who went from Super League to WWE as Ridge Holland. Luke explains how a tweet from William Regal led to a WWE tryout, what really happens inside the Performance Center, and the run of setbacks that followed, from blowing out both legs to foot surgery and a two-level artificial disc replacement in his neck. Now 38 and coaching online, he shares how he trains for longevity. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Ty Harrison on building Sengoku Martial Arts
summary: Ty Harrison is the founder of Sengoku Martial Arts in Featherstone. He started teaching karate under his dad in a school hall and went on to buy his own full-time academy. He tells Callum and Ryan how he outgrew his first unit, why his kids' classes run on a strict syllabus, how to ease nervous beginners into sparring, and the online marketing behind a second academy in Leeds. Plus the story of Patrick, who walked in at 12 and is now a pro kickboxer with three titles. Watch or read the full episode.

title: What new personal trainers get wrong about money
summary: Jay Johnston is a qualified accountant and coach who now works only with personal trainers, online coaches and gym owners as The Fitness Accountant. He tells Callum what he sees when PTs hand him their books: the first three financial things to do the day you start, why cash-in-hand coaching bites the moment you apply for a mortgage, sole trader versus limited company, whether to register for VAT, what you can genuinely put through the business, and why turnover is not profit. Watch or read the full episode.

title: AI, GLP-1s and the Death of the £20 Personal Trainer
summary: Recorded at PT Launch Lab Live, six people from across the fitness industry answer three questions: will AI replace personal trainers, are GLP-1 weight-loss drugs a threat or an opportunity for coaches, and is becoming a PT still worth it? On the panel: Sohail Rashid (Brawn), Tom Blackman (Ministry of Fitness), Chris Duffin, Jon Baker (Operations Director, The Gym Group), Jonny Grayshon and Paul Richardson (formerly Gymshark), hosted by Callum Brown and Miles Halstead. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Sohail Rashid: why in-person PT is AI-proof
summary: Sohail Rashid went from property lawyer and PropTech founder to competitive powerlifter and founder and CEO of the fitness-tech company Brawn. He explains how Brawn pivoted into virtual strength competitions during COVID and why he believes in-person personal training is an AI-proof career. The second half covers the traits of PTs who last, Hyrox versus proper strength training, Brawn's AI onboarding that matches new gym members to PTs, and why gyms need to be ready for GLP-1s and peptides. Watch or read the full episode.

title: What can a blood test reveal when you feel fine?
summary: Callum and Ryan sit down with James, a paramedic of 22 years who runs MyMedic Healthcare with two partners, to find out what private blood tests can show even when you feel fine. James explains why 90 of the first 100 results they reviewed had at least one marker worth improving, how overtraining shows up in your bloods, and the gym-goer whose high iron turned out to be haemochromatosis. They also cover TRT, women's hormones and the menopause, and how PTs could use blood testing with new clients. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Kim Tomlin on biomechanics and Primal Flows
summary: Kim Tomlin retrained as a personal trainer in her 30s, became a Primal Flows instructor a year later, went on to a biomechanics coaching diploma, and now teaches movement to other fitness professionals from Leeds. Callum Brown asks her why there is no single correct way to squat, why lower back pain often isn't a back problem, and who is harder to teach, clients or qualified PTs. They also cover whether the industry should be regulated and how to market yourself as a new trainer. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Miles Halstead: nearly 30 years in the gym industry
summary: Miles Halstead has spent close to 30 years in the fitness industry, from the Fitness First sales floor and running JJB's gyms in Scotland to selling his house to open MP Fit and now owning 6FitGyms. He tells Callum Brown why a gym should be a community 'third place', why what got you to 20 clients won't get you to 100, and why he expects a swing back to in-person personal training. He also shares what he looks for when hiring PTs and why new trainers shouldn't niche down too early. Watch or read the full episode.

title: What PureGym looks for when hiring PTs: Mac Livock
summary: Mac Livock, now a manager at PureGym, started out as the first self-employed PT at Ryan's gym in January 2020. He explains how he filled his diary fast just by being on the gym floor, what new trainers should charge, why he thinks you need gym-floor experience before going online, and why he moved into management when self-employment got in the way of a mortgage. He finishes with the two qualities he looks for when hiring: resilience and people skills. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Mistakes to avoid when starting a business: Sam
summary: Sam is the founder of Axol and Merve EdTech, the course platform PT Launch Lab was the first to go live on, and one of Callum's own PT clients. He shares the startup mistakes he wouldn't repeat - hiring too early, paying for lead generation too soon, building too much before launch - and why honesty, low costs and looking after your first customers matter in any business, personal training included. He finishes with what he looks for in a personal trainer as a client. Watch or read the full episode.

title: How much should a personal trainer charge?
summary: Ryan and Callum sit down in the new studio, one now a professional boxer preparing for his second pro fight, the other building PT Launch Lab full time. Ryan walks through every price rise he has made since starting at £10 an hour aged seventeen, why each one landed on a milestone rather than a date, and what happened when a client asked him to match a £20 session at the gym down the road. They also talk about treating a new client the way a mechanic treats a diagnostic, and what GLP-1s and steroids will and will not do. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Why personal trainers quit in the first two years
summary: Why do so many personal trainers leave the industry within their first two years? Callum Brown and Ryan Robinson break down the reasons, from inconsistent income and tax surprises to underpriced clients and burnout, and how to move from a job into self-employed PT without losing your safety net. Ryan also explains why he is closing the Shred fat-loss challenges after 10 years to focus on boxing and PT Launch Lab. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Is becoming a PT worth it? Is the UK market saturated?
summary: Is it still worth becoming a personal trainer in the UK when social media is full of laptop coaches in Dubai? Callum Brown and Ryan Robinson take on market saturation, why Ryan has stayed one of the busiest PTs in Pontefract for 13 years without leaving town, and why who you are matters more than any method. They also cover working two jobs while you build, setting limits on your hours, and what Ryan would do differently if he started again. Watch or read the full episode.

title: How Ryan built an online business from a challenge
summary: Ryan Robinson's online business began with a £30-a-head weight loss competition he ran to fill his PT diary, which grew until there were queues out of the gym. When lockdown hit he took it online and sold over a thousand places overnight, writing every diet plan by hand, before a split with a business partner forced him to start again. The second half is practical: you are the brand, how to answer price questions, the unpaid hours, and why you should never discount. Watch or read the full episode.

title: New Year fitness goals without burning out
summary: Ryan Robinson and Callum Brown look back on a year of closing and opening businesses, five fights and a growing podcast, and set their goals out loud: a professional boxing licence, strength competitions, a triathlon and 20 partner gyms. Then the practical part: why beginners should start with one small habit instead of overhauling everything in January, and why new personal trainers shouldn't beast January clients or drop their prices. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Good vs bad PT clients: the red flags every PT meets
summary: What separates a client who is a joy to coach from one who drains your time? Callum Brown and Ryan Robinson talk about clients who want to be there versus those who feel they need to be, how to keep someone going after a wedding or holiday goal, and why new clients can overtrain in the first few weeks. Then the red flags: arguments over missed sessions, block bookings stretched for months, and clients who never act on your advice. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Will AI replace personal trainers?
summary: Callum and Ryan talk through how AI is already changing the fitness industry: what it is genuinely good at, like building programmes, nutrition plans and saving admin time, and what it can't do, like being there for a client on a bad day. They also look at which online coaches are most at risk, how PT marketing has changed since the early Facebook days, and where holograms and smart glasses could take coaching next. Watch or read the full episode.

title: Are fitness influencers good role models for new PTs?
summary: Callum and Ryan get into fitness influencers and who new personal trainers should actually learn from. They talk about straight-talking influencers like James Smith, why copying the swearing looks unprofessional, how to give advice without telling people they're doing it wrong, and whether a personal trainer needs to be in shape. Plus internal versus external coaching cues, and why you can't reinvent the wheel. Watch or read the full episode.

title: The unsociable hours of a personal trainer
summary: A short, honest clip on the hours nobody warns you about when you become a personal trainer. A day that starts at 7am and runs into the evening: out before the kids go to school, missing them after school, and getting home just as they go to bed. Callum and Ryan explain why, especially in the early stages of building your own business, you have to put the hours in, and why they are rarely the hours you would choose. Watch or read the full episode.
